title: حِكَايَةُ الشَّيْخِ الْأَوَّلِ وَغَزَالَتِهِ، وَالشَّيْخِ الثَّانِي وَكَلْبَيْهِ، وَالشَّيْخِ الثَّالِثِ وَبَغْلَتِهِ
titleEn: The First Sheikh and His Gazelle, the Second Sheikh and His Two Dogs, and the Third Sheikh and His Mule
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 14–20, transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the project’s own two-pass-plus-adjudication pipeline; the edition’s own OCR is unusable. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition’s — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved unaltered, including two places (printed pp. 17) where a wa- proclitic was set at the very end of a printed line and its host word continues on the next; both are kept as the two separate tokens the edition itself prints. Read-aloud audio, where it exists elsewhere in this library, follows the convention of a Modern Standard Arabic reading; none is attached to this file yet.
about: This night finishes the First Sheikh’s tale of the enchanted calf and the gazelle who is his own cousin, then gives in full the Second Sheikh’s tale of his two brothers turned into dogs by his wife, a jinniyah, and the Third Sheikh’s tale of the wife who turned her unfaithful husband into a dog and was in turn transformed into a mule; each tale wins its teller a further third of the pardon owed the frame’s own condemned merchant, until the jinni forgives him outright. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language toward Classical Arabic here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit. Non-Classical forms and a few probable compositor’s slips are vocalized as printed and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. The tales are frank about magic, violence, and adultery, and are translated that way.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ قَالَتْ دُنْيَازَادُ لِأُخْتِهَا شَهْرَزَادَ يَا أُخْتِي أَتِمِّي لَنَا حَدِيثَكِ الَّذِي هُوَ حَدِيثُ التَّاجِرِ وَالْجِنِّيِّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāniyatu qālat Dunyāzādu li-ukhtihā Shahrazāda yā ukhtī atimmī lanā ḥadīthaki alladhī huwa ḥadīthu al-tājiri wa-al-jinniyyi
sentences.l: And when it was the second night, Dunyazad said to her sister Shahrazad: 'O my sister, complete for us your story, which is the story of the merchant and the jinni.'
sentences.i: When the second night came, Dunyazad said to her sister Shahrazad, 'O my sister, finish for us your tale -- the story of the merchant and the jinni.'
sentences.n: This formula -- 'and when it was the Nth night...' -- opens every night from here on; Night One, being first, simply announced itself instead (see its own note). Dunyazad is Shahrazad's younger sister, who by arrangement sleeps in the royal chamber and prompts her each dawn to keep the story going past daybreak.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ حُبًّا وَكَرَامَةً إِنْ أَذِنَ لِيَ الْمَلِكُ
sentences.tr: qālat ḥubban wa-karāmatan in adhina liya al-maliku
sentences.l: She said: 'With love and honor, if the King permits me.'
sentences.i: She said, 'Gladly and with honor -- if the King permits me.'
sentences.n: hubban wa-karamatan, literally 'with love and with honor', is a fixed formula of gracious, willing acceptance -- closer to 'most gladly' than to any comment on affection.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ اِحْكِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku iḥkī
sentences.l: The King said: 'Narrate!'
sentences.i: The King said, 'Tell it.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ وَالْوَلِيُّ الرَّشِيدُ أَنَّهُ لَمَّا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَذْبَحَ الْعِجْلَ حَنَّ قَابُهُ وَقَالَ لِلرَّاعِي أَبْقِ هَذَا الْعِجْلَ بَيْنَ الْبَهَائِمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu wa-al-waliyyu al-rashīdu annahu lammā arāda an yadhbaḥa al-ʿijla ḥanna qābuhu wa-qāla li-al-rāʿī abqi hādhā al-ʿijla bayna al-bahāʾ imi
sentences.l: She said: 'It has reached me, O happy King, the rightly-guided custodian, that when he wished to slaughter the calf, his qab (see note) softened, and he said to the herdsman: "Leave this calf among the cattle."'
sentences.i: She said, 'It is told, O happy King, guided rightly, that when he meant to slaughter the calf, his heart was moved with pity, and he said to the herdsman, "Leave this calf among the herd."'
sentences.n: This resumes a tale-within-a-tale already under way from Night One: an old man -- the 'owner of the gazelle' -- is recounting to a jinni (inside the merchant's own story) how he once kept a calf that turns out to be no ordinary animal. The rasm here reads q-a-b-h, short of the lam that 'his heart' (qalbuhu) would need; that is almost certainly what is meant ('his heart softened'), and it is pointed here to fit the printed letters as a probable compositor's slip rather than silently corrected.

sentences.t: كُلُّ ذَلِكَ وَالشَّيْخُ يَحْكِي إِلَى الْجِنِّيِّ وَالْجِنِّيُّ يَتَعَجَّبُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامِ الْعَجِيبِ
sentences.tr: kullu dhālika wa-al-shaykhu yaḥkī ilā al-jinniyyi wa-al-jinniyyu yataʿajjabu min dhālika al-kalāmi al-ʿajībi
sentences.l: All that while the old man was narrating to the jinni, and the jinni was marveling at that strange talk.
sentences.i: All this while the old man went on telling his tale to the jinni, who marveled at the strange account.
sentences.n: kullu dhalika wa-... ('all that while...') is a circumstantial construction marking two things happening at once; it recurs through the frame narration.

sentences.t: قَالَ صَاحِبُ الْغَزَالَةِ يَا سَيِّدَ مُلُوكِ الْجَانِّ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ جَرَى وَابْنَةُ عَمِّي هَذِهِ الْغَزَالَةُ تَنْظُرُ وَتَرَى وَتَقُولُ اِذْبَحِ الْعِجْلَ فَإِنَّهُ سَمِينٌ
sentences.tr: qāla ṣāḥibu al-ghazālati yā sayyida mulūki al-jānni kullu dhālika jarā wa-ibnatu ʿammī hādhihi al-ghazālatu tanẓuru wa-tarā wa-taqūlu idhbaḥi al-ʿijla fa-innahu samīnun
sentences.l: The owner of the gazelle said: 'O lord of the kings of the jinn, all that happened, while this gazelle -- my cousin -- was watching and seeing and saying: "Slaughter the calf, for it is fat."'
sentences.i: The owner of the gazelle said, 'O lord of the kings of the jinn, all this took place while this gazelle here, my own cousin, watched and kept saying, "Slaughter the calf -- it is fat."'
sentences.n: ibnatu 'ammi, 'my paternal uncle's daughter', is the standard term for a female first cousin; that this particular cousin is now a gazelle is the enchantment this speaker is about to explain.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَهُونُ عَلَيَّ أَنْ أَذْبَحَهُ وَأَمَرْتُ الرَّاعِيَ أَنْ يَأْخُذَهُ فَأَخَذَهُ وَتَوَجَّهَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yahūnu ʿalayya an adhbaḥahu wa-amartu al-rā˻iya an yaʾakhudhahu fa-akhadhahu wa-tawajjaha bihi
sentences.l: So it was not easy upon me that I slaughter it; and I ordered the herdsman to take it, and he took it and set off with it.
sentences.i: I could not bring myself to slaughter it, so I ordered the herdsman to take it away; he took it and went off with it.
sentences.n: yahunu is the plain indicative, not the classical jussive yahun expected after lam; the Nights regularly keeps weak verbs in their full form after negating particles rather than applying the classical apocopation -- a recurring Middle Arabic feature, not an error.

sentences.t: فَفِي ثَانِي الْيَوْمِ أَنَا جَالِسٌ وَإِذَا بِالرَّاعِي مُقْبِلٌ إِلَى عِنْدِي وَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي أَقُولُ لَكَ شَيْئًا تُسَرُّ بِهِ وَلِيَ الْبِشَارَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-fī thānī al-yawmi anā jālisun wa-idhā bi-al-rāʿī muqbilun ilā ʿindī wa-qāla yā sayyidī aqūlu laka shayʺn tusarru bihi wa-liya al-bishāratu
sentences.l: So on the second day I was sitting, and behold, the herdsman was coming toward me; and he said: 'O my master, I shall tell you something that will gladden you, and I have the good news.'
sentences.i: The next day, as I sat there, suddenly the herdsman came toward me and said, 'My master, let me tell you something that will delight you -- I have good news for you.'
sentences.n: wa-idha bi-, 'and behold, there was...', is the same startling-turn construction already met in the frame story and in Night One.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu naʿam
sentences.l: I said: 'Yes.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَيُّهَا التَّاجِرُ إِنَّ لِي بِنْتًا وَكَانَتْ تَعَلَّمَتِ السِّحْرَ فِي صِغَرِهَا مِنِ امْرَأَةٍ عَجُوزٍ كَانَتْ عِنْدَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ayyuhā al-tājiru inna lī bintan wa-kānat taʿallamati al-siḥra fī ṣighariha mini imraʾatin ʿajūzin kānat ʿindanā
sentences.l: He said: 'O merchant, I have a daughter, and she had learned sorcery in her youth from an old woman who was with us.'
sentences.i: He said, 'O merchant, I have a daughter; she had learned sorcery in her youth from an old woman who lived with us.'

sentences.t: فَلَمَّاكَانَ بِالْأَمْسِ وَأَعْطَيْتَنِي الْعِجْلَ دَخَلْتُ عَلَيْهَا فَنَظَرَتْ إِلَيْهِ بِنْتِي وَغَطَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَبَكَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna bi-al-amsi wa-aʿṭaytānī al-ʿijla dakhaltu ʿalayhā fa-naẓarat ilayhi bintī wa-ghaṭṭat wajhahā wa-bakat
sentences.l: Then yesterday, when you had given me the calf, I went in to her, and my daughter looked at it, and covered her face, and wept.
sentences.i: Then yesterday, when you gave me the calf, I went in to her, and my daughter looked at it, covered her face, and burst into tears.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا ضَحِكَتْ وَقَالَتْ يَا أَبَتِ بَخْسُ قَدْرِي عِنْدَكَ حَتَّى أَنَّكَ تُدْخِلُ عَلَيَّ الرِّجَالَ الْأَجَانِبَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā ḍaḥikat wa-qālat yā abati bakhsu qadrī ʿindaka ḥattā annaka tudkhilu ʿalayya al-rijāla al-ajāniba
sentences.l: Then she laughed and said: 'O my father, [how] my worth is diminished in your eyes, that you should bring in to me strange men!'
sentences.i: Then she laughed and said, 'O father, how little you must think of me, that you bring strange men in to me!'
sentences.n: bakhsu qadri is read here as a nominal exclamation ('the diminishing of my worth...!') since the printed rasm (three letters, b-kh-s) lacks the ending a finite verb 'you undervalued' would need; ya abati is the old vocative for 'father', using a vowelled ta where 'my brother' would use a possessive ya.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَأَيْنَ الرِّجَالُ الْأَجَانِبُ وَلِمَا ذَا بَكَيْتِ وَضَحِكْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā wa-ayna al-rijālu al-ajānibu wa-limā dhā bakayti wa-ḍaḥikti
sentences.l: I said to her: 'And where are the strange men? And why did you weep and laugh?'
sentences.i: I said to her, 'Where are these strange men? And why did you weep, then laugh?'

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِي إِنَّ هَذَا الْعِجْلَ الَّذِي مَعَكَ ابْنُ أُسْتَاذِنَا وَهُوَ مَسْحُورٌ وَقَدْ سَحَرَتْهُ زَوْجَةُ أَبِيهِ هُوَ وَأُمُّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lī inna hādhā al-ʿijla alladhī maʿaka ibnu ustādhinā wa-huwa masḥūrun wa-qad saḥarathu zawjatu abīhi huwa wa-ummuhu
sentences.l: She said to me: 'This calf that is with you is the son of our master, and he is enchanted; his father's wife has bewitched him -- him and his mother.'
sentences.i: She said to me, 'This calf you have is the son of our master; he is under a spell -- his father's wife has bewitched him, both him and his mother.'
sentences.n: 'Our master' is the speaker's own employer -- that is, the narrator himself; the herdsman's daughter does not yet know she is describing his own household to his face. 'His father' two lines on is likewise the narrator.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا سَبَبُ ضَحِكِي وَأَمَّا سَبَبُ بُكَائِي فَمِنْ أَجْلِ أَنَّهُ كَيْفَ ذَبَحَهَا أَبُوهُ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā sababu ḍaḥikī wa-ammā sababu bukāʾī fa-min ajli annahu kayfa dhabaḥahā abūhu
sentences.l: This then is the reason for my laughter; but as for the reason for my weeping, it is on account of how his father slaughtered her.
sentences.i: That is the reason for my laughing. But the reason for my weeping is over how his father came to slaughter her.
sentences.n: The 'her' slaughtered here is the boy's mother, transformed -- the listener now realizes that he himself, unknowingly, is the father in this account.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبْتُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ غَابَةَ الْعَجَبِ وَمَا صَدَّقْتُ بِطُلُوعِ الصَّبَاحِ حَتَّى جِئْتُ إِلَيْكَ أُعْلِمُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjabtu min dhālika ghābata al-ʿajabi wa-mā ṣaddaqtu bi-ṭulūʿi al-ṣabāḥi ḥattā jiʾtu ilayka uʿlimuka
sentences.l: And I marveled at that to the utmost of wonder, and I did not credit the break of morning until I came to you to inform you.
sentences.i: I marveled at this beyond all measure, and could scarcely believe day had broken before I came to tell you.
sentences.n: The rasm reads gh-a-b-h ('forest'), which cannot be right after 'the utmost of--'; this is almost certainly ghaya ('utmost degree'), a ba' misprinted for a ya', and is pointed and translated accordingly.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ أَيُّهَا الْجِنِّيُّ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ مِنَ الرَّاعِي خَرَجْتُ مَعَهُ وَأَنَا سَكْرَانُ مِنْ غَيْرِ مُدَامٍ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الْفَرَحِ وَالسُّرُورِ الَّذِي حَصَلَ لِي إِلَى أَنْ أَتَيْتُ إِلَى دَارِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu ayyuhā al-jinniyyu hādhā al-kalāma mina al-rāʿī kharajtu maʿahu wa-anā sakrānu min ghayri mudāmin min kathrati al-faraḥi wa-al-surūri alladhī ḥaṣala lī ilā an ataytu ilā dārihi
sentences.l: So when I heard, O jinni, this speech from the herdsman, I went out with him, while I was drunk without wine, from the abundance of the joy and gladness that had come upon me, until I came to his house.
sentences.i: When I heard this, O jinni, from the herdsman, I went out with him, drunk with joy though I had touched no wine -- so great was the happiness that had come over me -- until I reached his house.
sentences.n: 'Drunk without wine' is a set idiom for being overcome with joy.

sentences.t: فَتَرَحَّبَتْ بِي ابْنَةُ الرَّاعِي وَقَبَّلَتْ يَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-taraḥḥabat bī ibnatu al-rāʿī wa-qabbalat yadī
sentences.l: So the herdsman's daughter welcomed me, and kissed my hand.
sentences.i: The herdsman's daughter welcomed me warmly and kissed my hand.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعِجْلَ جَاءَ إِلَيَّ وَتَمَرَّغَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿijla jāʾa ilayya wa-tamaragha ʿalayya
sentences.l: Then the calf came to me and rolled about upon me.
sentences.i: Then the calf came up to me and rolled about at my feet.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لِابْنَةِ الرَّاعِي أَحَقٌّ مَا تَقُولِيهِ عَنْ ذَلِكَ الْعِجْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu li-ibnati al-rāʿī a-ḥaqqun mā taqūlīhi ʿan dhālika al-ʿijli
sentences.l: I said to the herdsman's daughter: 'Is what you say about that calf true?'
sentences.i: I asked the herdsman's daughter, 'Is what you say about that calf true?'
sentences.n: taquliihi keeps a Middle Arabic 2nd-feminine ending -i (rather than Classical -ina with the energetic nun, taqulinahu); the same pattern recurs just below in khallastiihi.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ نَعَمْ يَا سَيِّدِي إِنَّهُ ابْنُكَ وَحَشَاشَةُ كَبِدِكَ
sentences.tr: qālat naʿam yā sayyidī innahu ibnuka wa-ḥashāshatu kabidika
sentences.l: She said: 'Yes, my master, he is your son, and the fresh flesh of your liver.'
sentences.i: She said, 'Yes, my master -- he is your own son, the very core of your heart.'
sentences.n: 'The fresh flesh of your liver' (hashashatu kabidika) is a classical term of endearment for one's own dearest child, roughly 'your heart's blood'.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَيَّتُهَا الصَّبِيَّةُ إِنْ أَنْتِ خَلَّصْتِيهِ فَلَكِ عِنْدِي مَا تَحْتَ يَدِ أَبِيكِ مِنَ الْمَوَاشِي وَالْأَمْوَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā ayyatuhā al-ṣabiyyatu in anti khallaṣtīhi fa-laki ʿindī mā taḥta yadi abīki mina al-mawāshī wa-al-amwāli
sentences.l: I said to her: 'O girl, if you free him, then you shall have from me whatever is under your father's hand of cattle and wealth.'
sentences.i: I said to her, 'O girl, if you free him, you shall have from me all that is in your father's keeping -- the cattle and the wealth alike.'
sentences.n: khallastiihi again shows the Middle Arabic -ti ending noted above.

sentences.t: فَتَبَسَّمَتْ وَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي لَيْسَ لِي رَغْبَةٌ فِي الْمَالِ إِلَّا بِشَرْطَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-tabassamat wa-qālat yā sayyidī laysa lī raghbatun fī al-māli illā bi-sharaṭayni
sentences.l: So she smiled and said: 'O my master, I have no desire for the wealth, except on two conditions.'
sentences.i: She smiled and said, 'My master, I have no wish for the wealth, save on two conditions.'

sentences.t: الْأَوَّلُ أَنْ تُزَوِّجَنِي بِهِ وَالثَّانِي إِنَّ السِّحْرَ مَنْ سَحَرَتْهُ وَاحْبِسْهَا وَإِلَّا فَلَسْتُ آمِنًا مِنْ مَكْرِهَا
sentences.tr: al-awwalu an tuzawwijanī bihi wa-al-thānī anna al-siḥra man saḥarathu wa-iḥbis-hā wa-illā fa-lastu āminan min makrihā
sentences.l: The first: that you marry me to him. And the second: that the sorcery -- whoever performed it on him -- you confine her! Otherwise I am not safe from her cunning.
sentences.i: The first is that you give me to him in marriage. The second is that whoever worked this sorcery on him, you must imprison her -- for otherwise I can never be safe from her cunning.
sentences.n: tuzawwijani bihi uses the causative zawwaja ('to marry X off to Y'), not the reflexive 'to marry' -- she is asking to be given to the calf/boy in marriage, not to marry the narrator. The sentence also slips from an indirect 'that' clause into a direct command (ihbis-ha, 'imprison her!') -- a loose, spoken-register turn typical of the storytelling voice.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ أَيُّهَا الْجِنِّيُّ كَلَامَ بِنْتِ الرَّاعِي فَقُلْتُ وَلَكِ فَوْقَ مَا طَلَبْتِ جَمِيعُ مَا تَحْتَ يَدِ أَبِيكِ مِنَ الْأَنْعَامِ وَالْأَمْوَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu ayyuhā al-jinniyyu kalāma binti al-rāʿī fa-qultu wa-laki fawqa mā ṭalabti jamīʿu mā taḥta yadi abīki mina al-anʿāmi wa-al-amwāli
sentences.l: So when I heard, O jinni, the herdsman's daughter's words, I said: 'You shall have, beyond what you asked, all that is under your father's hand of cattle and wealth.'
sentences.i: When I heard, O jinni, the herdsman's daughter's words, I said, 'You shall have even more than you asked -- all that your father holds, the livestock and the wealth together.'

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا بِنْتُ عَمِّي فَلَحْمُهَا لَكِ مُبَاحٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā bintu ʿammī fa-laḥmuhā laki mubāḥun
sentences.l: As for my cousin, then her flesh is permitted to you.
sentences.i: And as for my cousin -- she is yours to deal with as you please.
sentences.n: 'Her flesh is permitted to you' licenses the sorceress to do with the gazelle-cousin as she likes, presumably in payment for undoing the spell.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامِي أَخَذَتْ طَاسَةً وَمَلَأَتْهَا مَاءًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmī akhadhat ṭāsatan wa-malaʾathā māʺn
sentences.l: Then, when she heard my words, she took a basin and filled it with water.
sentences.i: Hearing this, she took a basin and filled it with water.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا عَزَمَتْ عَلَيْهَا وَرَشَّتْ بِهِ الْعِجْلَ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنْ كُنْتَ عِجْلًا وَأَنْتَ عَلَى
sentences.tr: thumma innahā ʿazamat ʿalayhā wa-rashshat bihi al-ʿijla wa-qālat lahu in kunta ʿijlan wa-anta ʿalā
sentences.l: Then she recited a charge over it, and sprinkled the calf with it, and said to it: 'If you are a calf, and you are upon...'
sentences.i: Then she pronounced a charm over the water, sprinkled the calf with it, and said to it, 'If you are truly a calf, and you remain as you were...'
sentences.n: The archived slice breaks off here, mid-formula; the standard shape of such a spell ('if you are a calf by nature, keep this form -- but if you are enchanted, return to your own shape') evidently continues beyond this excerpt.

sentences.t: خِلْقَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى دَمٌ عَلَى هَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ وَلَا تَتَغَيَّرْ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مَسْحُورًا فَعُدْ إِلَى خِلْقَتِكَ الْأُولَى بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: khilqati Allāhi taʿālā damun ʿalā hādhihi al-ṣifati wa-lā tataghayyar wa-in kunta masḥūran fa-ʿud ilā khilqatika al-ūlā bi-idhni Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: …the creation of God, Exalted is He: blood, in this manner, and it does not change; but if you have been enchanted, then return to your first creation, by the permission of God, Exalted is He.
sentences.i: …by God's own creation, this is flesh and blood, just as it is — let it not change; but if you have been bewitched, return to your first form, by the leave of God, Exalted is He.
sentences.n: This sentence continues directly from the previous slice, where the herdsman's daughter, having sprinkled the calf, said: 'If you are truly a calf, being of the creation of God, Exalted is He...' — a single conditional charm covering both possibilities, ordinary animal or enchanted human, at once; the transformation in the next line answers which was true.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِهِ انْتَفَضَ وَصَارَ إِنْسَانًا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bihi intafaḍa wa-ṣāra insānan
sentences.l: And behold, he shook, and became a human being.
sentences.i: And all at once he shivered, and turned into a man.

sentences.t: فَوَقَعْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ احْكِ عَلَيَّ مَا صَنَعَتْ بِكَ بِنْتُ عَمِّي وَبِآمِّكَ
sentences.tr: fa-waqaʿtu ʿalayhi wa-qultu lahu bi-Allāhi ʿalayka iḥki ʿalayya mā ṣanaʿat bika bintu ʿammī wa-bi-āmmik
sentences.l: So I fell upon him, and said to him: 'By God upon you, tell me what my cousin did to you, and to your mother.'
sentences.i: So I threw myself upon him and said, 'I adjure you by God — tell me what my cousin did to you, and to your mother.'
sentences.n: وَبِآمِّكَ prints a precomposed hamza (آ) for what is read here as a colloquial contraction of بِأُمِّكَ, 'to your mother' — a Middle Arabic spelling kept exactly as the archive gives it rather than normalized to the Classical form.

sentences.t: فَحَكَى عَلَيَّ مَا جَرَى لَهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakā ʿalayya mā jarā lahumā
sentences.l: So he related to me what had happened to the two of them.
sentences.i: So he told me all that had befallen the two of them.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ يَا وَلَدِي قَدْ بَعَثَ اللَّهُ لَكَ مَنْ خَلَّصَكَ وَخَلَّصَ حَظَّكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu yā waladī qad baʿatha Allāhu laka man khallaṣaka wa-khallaṣa ḥaẓẓaka
sentences.l: So I said: 'O my son, God has indeed sent you one who delivered you and delivered your fortune.'
sentences.i: So I said, 'My son, God has truly sent you someone who has saved you, and secured your fortune with you.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَيُّهَا الْجِنِّيُّ زَوَّجْتُ ابْنَةَ الرَّاعِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma innī ayyuhā al-jinniyyu zawwajtu ibnata al-rāʿī bihi
sentences.l: Then indeed I, O jinni, married the herdsman's daughter to him.
sentences.i: Then, O jinni, I gave the herdsman's daughter to him in marriage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا سَحَرَتِ ابْنَةَ عَمِّي هَذِهِ الْغَزَالَةَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā saḥarati ibnata ʿammī hādhihi al-ghazālata
sentences.l: Then indeed she enchanted my cousin, this gazelle.
sentences.i: Then she — the very one — turned my cousin into this gazelle you see here.
sentences.n: The unnamed 'she' is the herdsman's daughter, just given to my son in marriage, now taking her revenge on the wife who had the boy and his mother enchanted; سَحَرَتْ here governs two accusatives (person, resulting shape), exactly as when the wife herself enchanted the boy and his mother earlier in this tale.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِي هَذِهِ صُورَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ لَيْسَتْ بِصُورَةٍ وَحْشِيَّةٍ يُكْرَهُ النَّظَرُ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lī hādhihi ṣūratun jamīlatun laysat bi-ṣūratin waḥshiyyatin yukrahu al-naẓaru ilayhā
sentences.l: And she said to me: 'This is a beautiful form, not a savage form, at which the looking is hated.'
sentences.i: And she said to me, 'This is a fair shape, not some hideous beast's shape that one would shrink from looking upon.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ بِنْتَ الرَّاعِي أَقَامَتْ عِنْدَنَا أَيَّامًا وَلَيَالِيَ وَلَيَالِيَ وَأَيَّامًا حَتَّى اخْتَارَهَا اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna binta al-rāʿī aqāmat ʿindanā ayyāman wa-layāliya wa-layāliya wa-ayyāman ḥattā ikhtārahā Allāhu ilayhi
sentences.l: Then indeed the herdsman's daughter dwelt with us days and nights, nights and days, until God chose her unto Himself.
sentences.i: Then the herdsman's daughter lived on with us for days and nights, nights on end and days, until God took her to Himself.
sentences.n: اخْتَارَهَا اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ, literally 'God chose her to Himself', is this text's euphemism for her death. The doubled, reversed phrase 'days and nights, nights and days' is a rhetorical flourish for the passage of a long time, echoing the rhymed-prose habits of this text even here in plain narration.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ أَنْ تُوُفِّيَتْ سَافَرَ ابْنِي إِلَى بِلَادِ الْهِنْدِ وَهِيَ بِلَادُ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي جَرَى لَكَ مَعَهُ مَا جَرَى
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda an tuwuffiyat sāfara ibnī ilā bilādi al-hindi wa-hiya bilādu hādhā al-rajuli alladhī jarā laka maʿahu mā jarā
sentences.l: And after she died, my son traveled to the lands of India — and it is the land of this man, with whom befell you what befell.
sentences.i: And after she died, my son set out for the land of India — the very land of this man here, the one with whom all that happened, happened.
sentences.n: This is the thread that ties the sheikh's own story back to the merchant's: his son's chosen destination turns out to be the merchant's homeland.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَخَذْتُ الْغَزَالَةَ بِنْتَ عَمِّي وَسِرْتُ بِهَا مِنْ بَلَدٍ إِلَى بَلَدٍ أُبْصِرُ خَبَرَ وَلَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika akhadhtu al-ghazālata binta ʿammī wa-sirtu bihā min baladin ilā baladin ubṣiru khabara waladī
sentences.l: So thereupon I took the gazelle, my cousin, and journeyed with her from land to land, that I might perceive news of my son.
sentences.i: So then I took the gazelle — my cousin — and traveled with her from land to land, seeking word of my son.
sentences.n: أُبْصِرُ here carries the sense of a purpose clause ('so that I might learn') with no subordinating particle at all — this narrative's habit of simply setting the imperfect verb in sequence rather than marking purpose overtly.

sentences.t: حَتَّى سَاقَتْنِي الْمَقَادِيرُ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ وَرَأَيْتُ التَّاجِرَ جَالِسًا يَبْكِي وَهَذَا حَدِيثِي
sentences.tr: ḥattā sāqatnī al-maqādīru ilā hādhā al-makāni wa-raʾaytu al-tājira jālisan yabkī wa-hādhā ḥadīthī
sentences.l: Until the fates drove me to this place, and I saw the merchant sitting weeping — and this is my story.
sentences.i: Until fate itself drove me to this very place, where I saw the merchant sitting and weeping — and that is my story.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْجِنِّيُّ هَذَا حَدِيثٌ عَجِيبٌ وَقَدْ وَهَبْتُ لَكَ ثُلُثَ دَمِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-jinniyyu hādhā ḥadīthun ʿajībun wa-qad wahabtu laka thulutha damihi
sentences.l: So the jinni said: 'This is a wondrous story; and I have granted you a third of his blood.'
sentences.i: The jinni said, 'That is indeed a wondrous tale — and I grant you a third of his blood.'

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَقَدَّمَ الشَّيْخُ الثَّانِي صَاحِبُ الْكَلْبَيْنِ السَّلُوقِيَّيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqaddama al-shaykhu al-thānī ṣāḥibu al-kalbayni al-salūqiyyayni
sentences.l: So thereupon the second sheikh, master of the two Saluki dogs, came forward.
sentences.i: Then the second sheikh, the owner of the two Saluki hounds, stepped forward.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِلْجِنِّيِّ إِنْ حَكَيْتُ لَكَ مَا جَرَى لِي مَعَ أَخَوَيَّ هَذَيْنِ الْكَلْبَيْنِ وَرَأَيْتَهَا أَغْرَبَ حِكَايَةً وَأَعْجَبَ تَهَبُ لِي ثُلُثَ ذَنْبِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-al-jinniyyi in ḥakaytu laka mā jarā lī maʿa akhawayya hādhayni al-kalbayni wa-raʾaytahā aghraba ḥikāyatan wa-aʿjaba tahabu lī thulutha dhanbihi
sentences.l: And he said to the jinni: 'If I relate to you what happened to me with these two brothers of mine, these two dogs, and you find it a stranger and more wondrous tale, will you grant me a third of his guilt?'
sentences.i: And he said to the jinni, 'If I tell you what happened to me with these two brothers of mine, these two dogs, and you find it a stranger, more marvelous tale — will you grant me a third of his due?'
sentences.n: The archive prints ذَنْب, 'sin, guilt', here rather than the دَم, 'blood', used for the same bargain elsewhere in this frame; vocalized as dhanb ('guilt') rather than dhanab ('tail', which the dogs might otherwise suggest), since 'his tail' cannot sensibly refer back to the merchant. Genuinely uncertain; flagged for the reviewer.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنْ كُنْتَ حِكَايَتُكَ أَعْجَبَ وَأَغْرَبَ فَلَكَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu in kunta ḥikāyatuka aʿjaba wa-aghraba fa-laka dhālika
sentences.l: So he said to him: 'If you — your story is more wondrous and stranger — then that is yours.'
sentences.i: He replied, 'If your story turns out more wondrous and stranger yet, then it is yours.'
sentences.n: إِنْ كُنْتَ حِكَايَتُكَ..., literally 'if you [were], your story [more wondrous]', is a loose construction in which كان agrees with the addressee rather than with the following noun clause's own subject; it recurs across the sheikhs' bargains in this night and is read as printed rather than emended to kānat.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الشَّيْخُ اعْلَمْ يَا سَيِّدَ مُلُوكِ الْجَانِّ أَنَّ هَذَيْنِ الْكَلْبَيْنِ إِخْوَتِي وَأَنَا ثَالِثُهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-shaykhu iʿlam yā sayyida mulūki al-jānni anna hādhayni al-kalbayni ikhwatī wa-anā thālithuhum
sentences.l: So the sheikh said to him: 'Know, O lord of the kings of the jinn, that these two dogs are my brothers, and I am the third of them.'
sentences.i: The sheikh said to him: 'Know, O lord of the kings of the jinn, that these two dogs are my brothers, and I am the third among them.'

sentences.t: وَمَاتَ وَالِدِي وَخَلَّفَ لَنَا ثَلٰثَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-māta wālidī wa-khallafa lanā thalāthata ālāfi dīnārin
sentences.l: And my father died, and left to us three thousand dinars.
sentences.i: And my father died, leaving us three thousand dinars.
sentences.n: ثلثة is the same defective spelling (a dropped medial alif) already met in ثَلٰثَة and ثَلٰثِين elsewhere in this frame, pointed here with the dagger alif rather than corrected.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحْتُ أَنَا دُكَّانًا أَبِيعُ فِيهِ وَأَشْتَرِي وَكَذَلِكَ الْإِخْوَانُ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ فَتَحَ دُكَّانًا
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥtu anā dukkānan abīʿu fīhi wa-ashtarī wa-kadhālika al-ikhwānu kullu wāḥidin fataḥa dukkānan
sentences.l: So I opened, I, a shop, in which I sell and buy; and likewise the brothers, each one opened a shop.
sentences.i: So I opened a shop of my own, buying and selling in it; and my brothers did the same — each one opened his own shop.

sentences.t: فَمَا تَعَلَّلْتُ كَثِيرًا إِلَّا وَأَخِي الْكَبِيرُ أَحَدُ هَؤُلَاءِ الْكَلْبَيْنِ بَاعَ مَتَاعَ دُكَّانِهِ بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ وَاشْتَرَى بَضَائِعَ وَمَتْجَرًا وَسَافَرَ فَغَابَ عَنَّا سَنَةً كَامِلَةً
sentences.tr: fa-mā taʿallaltu kathīran illā wa-akhī al-kabīru aḥadu hāʾulāʾi al-kalbayni bāʿa matāʿa dukkānihi bi-alfi dīnārin wa-ishtarā baḍāʾiʿa wa-matjaran wa-sāfara fa-ghāba ʿannā sanatan kāmilatan
sentences.l: And I had not lingered long, except that my elder brother — one of these two dogs — sold the goods of his shop for a thousand dinars, and bought merchandise and trade-goods, and traveled; and he was absent from us a whole year.
sentences.i: I had scarcely settled into this when my elder brother — one of these very dogs — sold off the stock of his shop for a thousand dinars, bought merchandise and trade-goods, and set off traveling; and he was gone from us a full year.
sentences.n: مَا…إِلَّا وَ, literally 'not…except that/but', is this text's idiom for 'no sooner had…than', built here with illā wa- rather than the ḥattā used for the same idiom elsewhere in the frame.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا يَوْمًا فِي دُكَّانِي إِذْ وَقَفَ عَلَيَّ سَائِلٌ فَقُلْتُ يَفْتَحُ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-anā yawman fī dukkānī idh waqafa ʿalayya sāʾilun fa-qultu yaftaḥu Allāhu
sentences.l: And I, one day, in my shop, when a beggar stopped before me, I said: 'God will open.'
sentences.i: One day, as I sat in my shop, a beggar stopped in front of me; I said, 'God will provide.'
sentences.n: يَفْتَحُ اللَّهُ, literally 'God will open [a way]', is the standard formula spoken to a beggar in place of alms — a polite refusal, not a blessing added to a gift.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي وَقَدْ بَكَى مَا بَقِيتَ تَعْرِفُنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī wa-qad bakā mā baqīta taʿrifunī
sentences.l: So he said to me, having wept: 'You have not remained knowing me?'
sentences.i: He said to me, weeping, 'Do you not know me any longer?'
sentences.n: مَا بَقِيتَ تَعْرِفُنِي, literally 'you did not remain knowing me', is the idiom for 'you no longer recognize me'.

sentences.t: فَحَقَّقْتُهُ وَإِذَا بِهِ أَخِي
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaqqaqtuhu wa-idhā bihi akhī
sentences.l: So I made certain of him, and behold, there he was — my brother.
sentences.i: So I looked closely at him — and there he was, my own brother.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَرَحَّبْتُ بِهِ وَطَلَعْتُ بِهِ إِلَى الدُّكَّانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-raḥḥabtu bihi wa-ṭalaʿtu bihi ilā al-dukkāni
sentences.l: So I rose, and welcomed him, and brought him up to the shop.
sentences.i: So I got up, welcomed him warmly, and brought him into the shop.

sentences.t: فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ حَالِهِ فَأَجَابَنِي لَا تَسْأَلْ لِأَنَّ الْمَالَ مَالٌ وَالْحَالَ حَالٌ
sentences.tr: fa-saʾaltuhu ʿan ḥālihi fa-ajābanī lā tasʾal li-anna al-māla mālun wa-al-ḥāla ḥālun
sentences.l: So I asked him about his condition, and he answered me: 'Do not ask — for wealth is wealth, and condition is condition.'
sentences.i: I asked him how he fared, and he answered, 'Do not ask — money comes and goes, and fortune is fortune.'
sentences.n: لَا تَسْأَلْ لِأَنَّ الْمَالَ مَالٌ وَالْحَالَ حَالٌ, literally 'do not ask, for wealth is wealth and condition is condition', is a resigned commonplace deflecting a question about loss or ruin — roughly 'such is life'.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ أَدْخَلْتُهُ الْحَمَّامَ وَأَلْبَسْتُهُ بَذْلَةً مِنْ مَلَابِسِي وَأَطْلَعْتُهُ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu adkhaltuhu al-ḥammāma wa-albastuhu badhlatan min malābisī wa-aṭlaʿtuhu ʿindī
sentences.l: So I rose; I brought him into the bathhouse, and dressed him in a suit from my own clothes, and brought him up to stay with me.
sentences.i: So I got up and took him to the bathhouse, dressed him in a suit of my own clothes, and kept him with me.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ كَشَفْتُ حِسَابِي وَبَيْعَ دُكَّانِي فَوَجَدْتُ قَدْ كَسَبْتُ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَرَأْسُ مَالِي أَلْفَيْ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: thumma kashaftu ḥisābī wa-bayʿa dukkānī fa-wajadtu qad kasabtu alfa dīnārin wa-raʾsu mālī alfay dīnārin
sentences.l: Then I examined my accounts and the selling of my shop, and I found that I had gained a thousand dinars, and the total of my capital was two thousand dinars.
sentences.i: Then I went over my accounts and the sale of my shop, and found that I had earned a thousand dinars, and that my capital now stood at two thousand dinars.
sentences.n: رَأْسُ مَالِي, literally 'the head of my capital', is the standing idiom for one's principal or total capital, formed the same way as رَأْسُ سَنَةٍ, 'the head of a year', elsewhere in this tale.

sentences.t: فَقَسَمْتُهُ بَيْنَ أَخِي وَبَيْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qasamtuhu bayna akhī wa-baynī
sentences.l: So I divided it between my brother and myself.
sentences.i: So I split it between my brother and me.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ لَهُ احْسُبْ أَنَّكَ مَا سَافَرْتَ وَلَا تَغَرَّبْتَ
sentences.tr: wa-qultu lahu iḥsub annaka mā sāfarta wa-lā tagharrabta
sentences.l: And I said to him: 'Reckon that you did not travel, nor did you go abroad.'
sentences.i: And I told him, 'Consider it as though you never traveled, and never went away.'

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهَا وَهُوَ فَرْحَانُ وَفَتَحَ لَهُ دُكَّانًا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhahā wa-huwa farḥānu wa-fataḥa lahu dukkānan
sentences.l: So he took it, he being joyful, and opened for himself a shop.
sentences.i: So he took it, overjoyed, and opened a shop of his own.

sentences.t: وَقُمْتُ أَيَّامًا وَلَيَالِيَ
sentences.tr: wa-qumtu ayyāman wa-layāliya
sentences.l: And I remained days and nights.
sentences.i: And so it went on for some days and nights.
sentences.n: قُمْتُ here, unlike its usual sense 'I rose, stood up', seems used loosely for 'I remained, carried on' — the same root spelled أَقَمْتُ ('I dwelt') elsewhere in this tale, but printed here without the initial alif; read as it stands rather than corrected.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَامَ أَخِي الثَّانِي وَهُوَ الذَّٰهِبُ الْآخَرُ بَاعَ مَا كَانَ عِنْدَهُ وَجَمِيعَ مَالِهِ وَأَرَادَ السَّفَرَ فَمَنَعْنَاهُ فَلَمْ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda dhālika qāma akhī al-thānī wa-huwa al-dhāhibu al-ākharu bāʿa mā kāna ʿindahu wa-jamīʿa mālihi wa-arāda al-safara fa-manaʿnāhu fa-lam
sentences.l: Then after that, my second brother arose — he being the other one to travel — and sold what he had, and all his property, and wanted to travel; and we forbade him, but not—
sentences.i: Then, after that, my second brother rose up — he too meaning to travel — and sold everything he owned, all his property, and made ready to leave; but we forbade him, yet—
sentences.n: The sentence breaks off at the slice boundary on فَلَمْ, 'but not/yet did not'; it continues beyond this excerpt as لَمْ يَمْتَنِعْ, 'he did not relent'. الذَّاهِب is read here for the printed الذهب, with its medial alif dropped as elsewhere in this text (compare ثلاثة), meaning 'the one going, the traveler' — parallel to the elder brother's journey earlier; read at face value the letters would spell 'the gold', which cannot sensibly describe a brother, so this reading is offered with real uncertainty and flagged for the reviewer.

sentences.t: يَمْتَنِعُ
sentences.tr: yamtaniʿu
sentences.l: ...he would not desist.
sentences.n: The final word of a sentence begun in the previous night's slice (not available here); the subject and the rest of the clause lie just before this excerpt, so the rendering here is necessarily provisional.

sentences.t: فَاشْتَرَى تِجَارَةً وَسَافَرَ مَعَ الْأَسْفَارِ وَغَابَ عَنَّا سَنَةً كَامِلَةً
sentences.tr: fa-ishtarā tijāratan wa-sāfara maʿa al-asfāri wa-ghāba ʿannā sanatan kāmilatan
sentences.l: So he bought merchandise, and traveled with the caravans, and was absent from us a whole year.
sentences.i: So he bought goods, set off with the caravans, and was gone from us for a full year.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَتَانِي كَمَا أَتَى أَخُوهُ الْكَبِيرُ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu atānī kamā atā akhūhu al-kabīru
sentences.l: Then indeed he came to me, just as his elder brother had come.
sentences.i: Then he came to me, just as his elder brother had come before him.
sentences.n: 'His elder brother' is the first of the narrator's two prodigal brothers, already returned home in the same fashion; the two are being treated in turn.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ يَا أَخِي آمَا نَصَحْتُكَ بِأَنْ لَا تُسَافِرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu yā akhī amā naṣaḥtuka bi-an lā tusāfira
sentences.l: So I said to him: 'O my brother, did I not counsel you not to travel?'
sentences.i: So I said to him, 'My brother, did I not warn you not to travel?'
sentences.n: The edition spells this reproachful particle amā with a madda, آما, kept precomposed as printed.

sentences.t: فَبَكَى وَقَالَ يَا أَخِي هَذَا مُقَدَّرُوهَا
sentences.tr: fa-bakā wa-qāla yā akhī hādhā muqaddarūhā
sentences.l: So he wept and said: 'O my brother, this is its allotted measure.'
sentences.i: He wept and said, 'My brother, such was fate's portion for me.'
sentences.n: مُقَدَّرُوهَا is obscure as it stands: apparently مُقَدَّر ('decreed, fated') plus some form of the 3fs suffix -hā, but the letter order (ر before و) matches no recognized pattern — مقدورها ('its fated lot') would be the expected word. Vocalized as printed; read loosely as 'such was my fated lot.'

sentences.t: أَنَا فَقِيرٌ لَمْ أَمْلِكِ الدِّرْهَمَ الْفَرْدَ عُرْيَانٌ مَا عَلَيَّ الْقَمِيصُ
sentences.tr: anā faqīrun lam amliki al-dirhama al-farda ʿuryānun mā ʿalayya al-qamīṣu
sentences.l: I am poor; I do not possess a single dirham; naked — there is not upon me the shirt.
sentences.i: I am a poor man; I do not own so much as a single dirham; I am naked, without even a shirt on my back.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُهُ أَيُّهَا الْجِنِّيُّ وَأَدْخَلْتُهُ الْحَمَّامَ وَأَلْبَسْتُهُ بَذْلَةً جَدِيدَةً مِنْ مَلَابِسِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtuhu ayyuhā al-jinniyyu wa-adkhaltuhu al-ḥammāma wa-albastuhu badhlatan jadīdatan min malābisī
sentences.l: So I took him — O jinni — and brought him into the bathhouse, and clothed him in a new suit from my own garments.
sentences.i: So I took him in hand, O jinni, brought him to the bathhouse, and dressed him in a fresh suit of my own clothes.
sentences.n: Addressing the jinni directly mid-tale ('O jinni', 'O ifrit') is this narrator's habit of breaking through his own story to speak to his present audience; it recurs several times below.

sentences.t: وَجِئْتُ بِهِ إِلَى دُكَّانِي فَأَكَلْنَا وَشَرِبْنَا
sentences.tr: wa-jiʾtu bihi ilā dukkānī fa-akalnā wa-sharibnā
sentences.l: and I came with him to my shop, and we ate and drank.
sentences.i: and I brought him to my shop, and we ate and drank.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَهُ قُلْتُ لَهُ يَا أَخِي أَعْمَلُ حِسَابَ دُكَّانِي فِي كُلِّ رَأْسِ سَنَةٍ مَرَّةً
sentences.tr: wa-baʿdahu qultu lahu yā akhī aʿmalu ḥisāba dukkānī fī kulli raʾsi sanatin marratan
sentences.l: and after that I said to him: 'O my brother, I do the accounting of my shop, at the head of every year, once.'
sentences.i: and after that I said to him, 'My brother, once every year I settle the accounts of my shop,
sentences.n: raʾs sana, 'the head of a year', is the same idiom for a year's turning met earlier in the frame story.

sentences.t: وَالَّذِي أَرَاهُ زَائِدًا هُوَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ladhī arāhu zāʾidan huwa baynī wa-baynaka
sentences.l: and whatever I see as surplus, it is between me and you.'
sentences.i: and whatever I find over and above is shared between the two of us.'
sentences.n: زايدا drops the hamza sign from its own correct ي seat (for زائدًا); the same drop-and-restore treatment as رَأْس and شَاطِئ below.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ أَيُّهَا الْعِفْرِيتُ وَعَمِلْتُ حِسَابَ دُكَّانِي فَرَأَيْتُ أَلْفَيْ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu ayyuhā al-ʿifrītu wa-ʿamiltu ḥisāba dukkānī fa-raʾaytu alfay dīnārin
sentences.l: So I arose — O ifrit — and did the accounting of my shop, and I found two thousand dinars.
sentences.i: So I got up, O ifrit, and reckoned the accounts of my shop, and found two thousand dinars.

sentences.t: فَحَمِدْتُ الْبَارِيَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-ḥamidtu al-bāriya subḥānahu wa-taʿālā
sentences.l: So I praised the Creator, glorified and exalted is He.
sentences.i: So I gave praise to the Creator, glory and exaltation be His.

sentences.t: فَأَعْطَيْتُ أَخِي أَلْفًا وَبَقِيَ مَعِي أَلْفٌ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿṭaytu akhī alfan wa-baqiya maʿī alfun
sentences.l: So I gave my brother a thousand, and a thousand remained with me.
sentences.i: So I gave my brother a thousand, and kept a thousand for myself.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ أَخِي وَفَتَحَ دُكَّانًا وَقَعَدْنَا جُمْلَةَ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma akhī wa-fataḥa dukkānan wa-qaʿadnā jumlata ayyāmin
sentences.l: So my brother arose and opened a shop, and we sat a good number of days.
sentences.i: So my brother got up, opened a shop, and we went on so for a good while.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ مُدَّةٍ قَامُوا عَلَيَّ إِخْوَتِي وَأَرَادُوا أَنْ أُسَافِرَ وَإِيَّاهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda muddatin qāmū ʿalayya ikhwatī wa-arādū an usāfira wa-iyyāhum
sentences.l: Then, after a time, my brothers rose up against me, and wanted that I travel, and they with [me].
sentences.i: Then, after a while, my brothers began pressing me, wanting me to travel along with them.
sentences.n: qāmū ʿalayya, 'they rose up against/upon me', is the idiom for insistent pressuring rather than literal standing.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ فِعْلٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma fiʿlun
sentences.l: So — a deed came about.
sentences.i: So, in the end, I agreed.
sentences.n: فقام فعل is opaque as printed: a bare verb 'he arose' followed by the noun/verb 'deed/he did', with no clear subject or object. It may telescope a first-person 'so I did as they wished' (perhaps fa-qultu afʿalu or fa-faʿaltu), matching the agreement that follows — but this is a guess, not a restoration, and is flagged for the reviewer.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ أَيْشَ كَسَبْتُمْ أَنْتُمْ فِي سَفَرِكُمْ حَتَّى أَكْسِبَ أَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qultu lahum aysh kasabtum antum fī safarikum ḥattā aksiba anā
sentences.l: and I said to them: 'What did you gain, you, in your travel, that I should gain?'
sentences.i: and I said to them, 'What have you ever earned from your travels, that I should earn anything from mine?'
sentences.n: aysh, 'what', is the colloquial contraction of ay shayʾ ('which thing') standing throughout this tale for Classical mādhā; it recurs once more below.

sentences.t: فَمَا سَمِعْتُ مِنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-mā samiʿtu minhum
sentences.l: But I did not hear from them.
sentences.i: But I paid them no heed.
sentences.n: samiʿa min, literally 'to hear from', is the idiom for heeding or obeying someone.

sentences.t: وَأَقَمْنَا فِي دَكَاكِينِنَا نَبِيعُ وَنَشْتَرِي وَهُمْ يَعْرِضُونَ عَلَيَّ السَّفَرَ كُلَّ سَنَةٍ وَأَنَا لَا أَرْضَى
sentences.tr: wa-aqamnā fī dakākīninā nabīʿu wa-nashtarī wa-hum yaʿriḍūna ʿalayya al-safara kulla sanatin wa-anā lā arḍā
sentences.l: And we remained in our shops, selling and buying, while they proposed to me the travel every year, and I would not consent.
sentences.i: So we stayed on in our shops, buying and selling, while every year they urged me to travel, and every year I refused.

sentences.t: حَتَّى مَضَتْ لَنَا سِتَّةُ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: ḥattā maḍat lanā sittatu sinīna
sentences.l: until six years passed for us.
sentences.i: until six years had gone by.

sentences.t: فَأَنْعَمْتُ لَهُمْ بِالسَّفَرِ وَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ يَا إِخْوَتِي هَا أَنَا مُسَافِرٌ مَعَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-anʿamtu lahum bi-al-safari wa-qultu lahum yā ikhwatī hā anā musāfirun maʿakum
sentences.l: So I graciously granted them the travel, and said to them: 'O my brothers, here I am, traveling with you.'
sentences.i: So at last I gave in and agreed to travel, and said to them, 'My brothers, very well — here I am, ready to travel with you,

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ هَاتُوا لِكَيْ نَنْظُرَ أَيْشَ مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin hātū li-kay nanẓura aysh maʿakum mina al-māli
sentences.l: but bring [it], so that we may see what you have of money.'
sentences.i: but first bring out what money you have, so we may see it.'
sentences.n: hātū, 'bring! give!', is a defective imperative verb with no ordinary triliteral conjugation of its own.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَجِدِ مَعَهُمْ شَيْئًا بَلْ وَدَّرُوا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lam ajidi maʿahum shayʾan bal waddarū kulla shayʾin
sentences.l: But I found nothing with them; rather, they had squandered everything.
sentences.i: But I found nothing at all with them — they had squandered every bit of it.
sentences.n: waddarū, 'they squandered', is the Egyptian colloquial verb waddara (to waste money), not a Classical root; vocalized as the text's own word rather than corrected to a Classical equivalent like baddarū.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا مُتَعَكِّفِينَ عَلَى الْأَكْلِ وَ الشُّرْبِ وَالْمَلَذَّاتِ
sentences.tr: li-annahum kānū mutaʿakkifīna ʿalā al-akli wa al-shurbi wa-al-malaḏḏāti
sentences.l: because they had been devoted to eating and drinking and pleasures.
sentences.i: because they had done nothing but give themselves over to eating, drinking, and pleasure.
sentences.n: The archive's line breaks here so that wa- is printed alone at the end of one line and its noun begins the next (ʿalā al-akli wa / al-shurbi); the two are kept as the archive's own separate tokens rather than rejoined.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَلَّمْتُهُمْ وَلَا قُلْتُ لَهُمْ شَيْئًا
sentences.tr: fa-mā kallamtuhum wa-lā qultu lahum shayʾan
sentences.l: So I did not speak to them, nor did I say anything to them.
sentences.i: So I said nothing to them, not a word,

sentences.t: بَلْ قُمْتُ عَمِلْتُ حِسَابَ دُكَّانِي
sentences.tr: bal qumtu ʿamiltu ḥisāba dukkānī
sentences.l: rather I arose [and] did the accounting of my shop,
sentences.i: but simply went and reckoned the accounts of my own shop,

sentences.t: وَخَلَّيْتُ مَا عِنْدِي مِنَ الْمَالِ وَكُلَّ مَاكَانَ عِنْدِي مِنَ الْبَضَائِعِ
sentences.tr: wa-khallaytu mā ʿindī mina al-māli wa-kulla mā-kāna ʿindī mina al-baḍāʾiʿi
sentences.l: and gathered together what I had of money, and all that which was with me of goods,
sentences.i: gathered up all the money I had and all the merchandise in my possession,
sentences.n: khallaytu here carries the sense 'I set aside, I gathered together' — a use of Middle Arabic khallā wider than its Classical meaning 'to leave, to let alone'.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُ مَعِي سِتَّةَ أَلَافِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtu maʿī sittata alāfi dīnārin
sentences.l: So I found with me six thousand dinars,
sentences.i: and found that I had six thousand dinars in all.
sentences.n: The edition here spells 'thousands' without the madda it prints two lines below for the same word (آلاف); its hamza is supplied as a combining mark on the bare alif, the same drop-and-restore pattern as رَأْس and شَاطِئ.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحْتُ وَقُمْتُ قَسَمْتُهَا نِصْفَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥtu wa-qumtu qasamtuhā niṣfayni
sentences.l: So I rejoiced, and I arose [and] divided it into two halves,
sentences.i: I was overjoyed, and got up and divided it into two equal halves,

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ هَذِهِ، ثَلٰثَةُ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ لِي وَلَكُمْ لِكَيْ نَتَاجَرَ بِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qultu lahum hādhihi, thalāthatu ālāfi dīnārin lī wa-lakum li-kay natājara bihā
sentences.l: and said to them: 'This — three thousand dinars — is mine and yours, that we may trade with it.'
sentences.i: and said to them, 'Here — three thousand dinars are for the two of us, to trade with,
sentences.n: The edition prints ثلثة for thalātha throughout, without its medial alif; pointed here with the dagger alif, which reads correctly and strips back to the rasm as printed.

sentences.t: وَقُمْتُ دَفَنْتُ الثَّلٰثَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ الْأُخْرَى
sentences.tr: wa-qumtu dafantu al-thalāthata ālāfi dīnārin al-ukhrā
sentences.l: and I arose [and] buried the other three thousand dinars,
sentences.i: and the other three thousand I went and buried,

sentences.t: اِحْتِمَالًا أَنْ يَجْرِيَ عَلَيَّ مَا جَرَى عَلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: iḥtimālan an yajriya ʿalayya mā jarā ʿalayhim
sentences.l: as a possibility that there occur to me what occurred to them,
sentences.i: in case what had happened to them should happen to me too,

sentences.t: فَاجِي ثَلٰثَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ نَفْتَحُ بِهَا دَكَاكِينَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-ajī thalāthata ālāfi dīnārin naftaḥu bihā dakākīnanā
sentences.l: so [that] I come by three thousand dinars, [with which] we open our shops.'
sentences.i: so that I would still have three thousand dinars to open our shops with again.'
sentences.n: ajī is the colloquial Egyptian verb 'to come' (yijī/ajī), used here loosely for 'to come by, to have on hand' — a different verb from Classical jāʾa, not a spelling variant of it.

sentences.t: وَاِرْتَضَوْا كُلُّهُمْ فَأَعْطَيْتُ كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-irtaḍaw kulluhum fa-aʿṭaytu kulla wāḥidin alfa dīnārin
sentences.l: And they all agreed, and I gave each one a thousand dinars,
sentences.i: They all agreed to this, and I gave each of them a thousand dinars,

sentences.t: وَبَقِيَ لِي مِثْلُهُمْ أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-baqiya lī mithluhum alfu dīnārin
sentences.l: and there remained to me, like them, a thousand dinars.
sentences.i: keeping a thousand dinars for myself, the same as each of them.

sentences.t: فَتَحَوَّجْنَا الْبَضَائِعَ الْوَاجِبَةَ وَجَهَّزْنَا الْمُسْفَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-taḥawwajnā al-baḍāʾiʿa al-wājibata wa-jahhaznā al-musfara
sentences.l: So we procured the necessary goods, and we made ready [our] travel-gear,
sentences.i: So we laid in the goods we needed and made everything ready for the journey,
sentences.n: taḥawwajnā ('we sought out, procured what was needed'), from ḥāja ('need'), and al-musfar used here as a noun for the journey's preparations rather than 'the traveler', are both this narrator's own non-Classical usages.

sentences.t: وَ أَكْرَيْنَا مَرْكَبًا وَنَقَلْنَا فِيهِ حَوَايِجَنَا وَسَافَرْنَا أَوَّلَ يَوْمٍ وَثَانِيَ يَوْمٍ مُدَّةَ شَهْرٍ كَامِلٍ
sentences.tr: wa akraynā markaban wa-naqalnā fīhi ḥawāyijanā wa-sāfarnā awwala yawmin wa-thāniya yawmin muddata shahrin kāmilin
sentences.l: and [we] hired a ship, and moved into it our belongings, and we traveled, the first day and the second day, for the space of a whole month,
sentences.i: and we hired a ship, loaded our belongings into it, and set sail — day after day, for a full month,
sentences.n: ḥawāyij is the colloquial plural of ḥāja ('need, thing needed'), used here for 'belongings, effects', rather than the Classical plural ḥājāt.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلْنَا مَدِينَةً وَمَعَنَا بَضَائِعُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalnā madīnatan wa-maʿanā baḍāʾiʿunā
sentences.l: then we entered a city, with us our goods,
sentences.i: until we put in at a city, our merchandise still with us,

sentences.t: فَرَبِحْنَا فِي الدِّينَارِ عَشَرَةَ دَنَانِيرَ وَأَرَدْنَا نُسَافِرَ
sentences.tr: fa-rabiḥnā fī al-dīnāri ʿasharata danānīra wa-aradnā nusāfira
sentences.l: and we profited, on the dinar, ten dinars, and we wanted [that] we travel [further],
sentences.i: and made a profit of tenfold on every dinar; and we were minded to sail on
sentences.n: aradnā nusāfira drops the connecting an before the subjunctive (aradnā [an] nusāfira) — a common looseness of this text's spoken-register syntax.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْنَا عَلَى شَاطِئِ الْبَحْرِ جَارِيَةً عَلَيْهَا خِلْقَةٌ مُقَطَّعَةٌ فَقَبَّلَتْ يَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-wajadnā ʿalā shāṭiʾi al-baḥri jāriyatan ʿalayhā khilqatun muqaṭṭaʿatun fa-qabbalat yadī
sentences.l: when we found upon the shore of the sea a young woman, upon her a garment cut to pieces, and she kissed my hand,
sentences.i: when we found on the seashore a young woman dressed in tattered rags, who came and kissed my hand
sentences.n: jāriya here is a young woman (its base sense is 'slave-girl', but nothing else marks her as one); khilqa muqaṭṭaʿa, 'a garment cut to pieces', describes rags.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي هَلْ فِيكَ حَسَنَةٌ وَمَعْرُوفٌ أُجَازِيكَ عَلَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat yā sayyidī hal fīka ḥasanatun wa-maʿrūfun ujāzīka ʿalayhimā
sentences.l: and said: 'O my lord, is there in you a kindness and a favor [that] I may reward you for the two of them?'
sentences.i: and said, 'My lord, have you kindness and charity in you, that I might repay you for both?'

sentences.t: قُلْتُ نَعَمْ إِنِّي أُحِبُّ الْحَسَنَةَ، وَالْمَعْرُوفَ وَإِنْ لَمْ تُجَازِينِي
sentences.tr: qultu naʿam innī uḥibbu al-ḥasanata, wa-al-maʿrūfa wa-in lam tujāzīnī
sentences.l: I said: 'Yes, indeed I love kindness and favor, even if you do not reward me.'
sentences.i: I said, 'Yes — I love doing kindness and good, even should you never repay me.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي تَزَوَّجْنِي وَخُذْنِي بِلَادَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā sayyidī tazawwajnī wa-khudhnī bilādaka
sentences.l: So she said: 'O my lord, marry me, and take me to your country.'
sentences.i: She said, 'My lord, marry me, and take me to your own country,

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي قَدْ وَهَبْتُ نَفْسِي لَكَ فَاِفْعَلْ مَعِي مَعْرُوفًا
sentences.tr: fa-innī qad wahabtu nafsī laka fa-ifʿal maʿī maʿrūfan
sentences.l: for indeed I have given my very self to you; so do me a kindness,
sentences.i: for I have given myself over to you; so grant me this kindness.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا أَنَا مِمَّنْ يَفْعَلُ مَعَهُ الْمَعْرُوفُ وَالْحَسَنَةُ وَأُجَازِيكَ عَلَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā anā mimman yafʿalu maʿahu al-maʿrūfu wa-al-ḥasanatu wa-ujāzīka ʿalayhimā
sentences.l: As for me, I am one with whom kindness and favor are done, and I shall reward you for the two of them,
sentences.i: for I am one to whom kindness and favor are done in return — I shall repay you for both,
sentences.n: The turn is on ammā anā ('as for me'): she means that she herself is deserving of such kindness and will repay it — not, as the word order might first suggest, that she is the one who does kindness to others.

sentences.t: وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ حَالِي
sentences.tr: wa-lā yaghurrannaka ḥālī
sentences.l: and let not my condition deceive you,
sentences.i: and do not let my present state deceive you.
sentences.n: yaghurrannaka, with the emphatic nūn, is a warning: 'let it by no means deceive you' — she means her ragged appearance should not make him doubt what she can offer in return.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu
sentences.l: And when I heard...
sentences.i: And when I heard this...
sentences.n: The sentence breaks off here at the slice boundary; its continuation follows in the next portion of the tale.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَنَّ لَهَا قَلْبِي لِأَمْرٍ يُرِيدُهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فَأَخْدِمُهَا وَكَسَوْتُهَا وَفَرَشْتُ لَهَا فِي الْمَرْكَبِ فَرْشًا حَسَنًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥanna lahā qalbī li-amrin yurīduhu Allāhu ʿazza wa-jalla fa-akhdimuhā wa-kasawtuhā wa-farashtu lahā fī al-markabi farshan ḥasanan
sentences.l: So when my heart inclined tenderly toward her, for a matter God — Mighty and Majestic — willed, I serve her and clothed her and I spread for her, on the ship, fine bedding.
sentences.i: When my heart was moved with tenderness for her, for a purpose God, Mighty and Glorious, intended, I saw to her needs, clothed her, and laid out fine bedding for her aboard the ship.
sentences.n: fa-akhdimuhā slips into the present tense amid a run of past-tense verbs — a vivid 'narrative present' this text uses now and then; the idiomatic layer smooths it back to a simple past.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلْتُ عَلَيْهَا وَأَكْرَمْتُهَا وَسَافَرْنَا وَقَدْ أَحَبَّهَا قَلْبِي مَحَبَّةً عَظِيمَةً
sentences.tr: wa-aqbaltu ʿalayhā wa-akramtuhā wa-sāfarnā wa-qad aḥabbahā qalbī maḥabbatan ʿaẓīmatan
sentences.l: And I turned attentively to her, and treated her generously, and we traveled; and my heart had already loved her with a great love.
sentences.i: I turned my whole attention to her and treated her generously, and we set out on our journey; by then my heart had come to love her deeply.

sentences.t: وَصِرْتُ لَا أُفَارِقُهَا لَيْلًا وَلَا نَهَارًا وَاشْتَغَلْتُ بِهَا عَنْ إِخْوَتِي فَغَارُوا مِنِّي
sentences.tr: wa-ṣirtu lā ufāriquhā laylan wa-lā nahāran wa-ishtaghaltu bihā ʿan ikhwatī fa-ghārū minnī
sentences.l: And I became one who does not part from her, by night nor by day, and I occupied myself with her, away from my brothers, so they grew jealous of me.
sentences.i: I became inseparable from her, night and day, and let her occupy all my attention to the neglect of my brothers, until they grew jealous of me.

sentences.t: وَحَسَدُونِي عَلَى مَالِي وَكَثْرَةِ بِضَاعَتِي فَسُيِّرَتْ عُيُونُهُمْ فِي الْمَالِ جَمِيعِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥasadūnī ʿalā mālī wa-kathrati biḍāʿatī fa-suyyirat ʿuyūnuhum fī al-māli jamīʿihi
sentences.l: And they envied me for my wealth and the abundance of my merchandise, so their eyes were made to rove over all the wealth.
sentences.i: They envied me my wealth and my abundant merchandise, until their eyes could fix on nothing but all of it.
sentences.n: fa-suyyirat ʿuyūnuhum, literally 'their eyes were set roving', is this text's idiom for covetous fixation — they could not look away from it.

sentences.t: فَتَحَدَّثُوا فِي قَتْلِي وَأَخْذِ مَالِي وَقَالُوا نَقْتُلُ أَخَانَا وَيَصِيرُ الْمَالُ جَمِيعُهُ لَنَا وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمْ الشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-taḥaddathū fī qatlī wa-akhdhi mālī wa-qālū naqtulu akhānā wa-yaṣīru al-mālu jamīʿuhu lanā wa-zayyana lahum al-shayṭānu aʿmālahum
sentences.l: So they spoke together of killing me and taking my wealth, and they said: 'Let us kill our brother, and all the wealth will become ours.' And Satan made their deeds seem fair to them.
sentences.i: They fell to talking of killing me and seizing my wealth, saying, 'Let us kill our brother, and all his wealth will be ours.' So Satan made their scheme seem good to them.

sentences.t: وَخَلَّوْنِي وَأَنَا نَائِمٌ بِجَانِبِ زَوْجَتِي وَحَمَلُونِي وَزَوْجَتِي وَرَمَوْنَا فِي الْبَحْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-khallawnī wa-anā nāʾimun bi-jānibi zawjatī wa-ḥamalūnī wa-zawjatī wa-ramawnā fī al-baḥri
sentences.l: And they left me be, while I was asleep beside my wife; and they carried me and my wife, and cast us into the sea.
sentences.i: They caught me off guard, asleep beside my wife, then carried the two of us off and threw us into the sea.
sentences.n: khallawnī (form II of khalā) is used here as 'they left me alone, let me be' — a Middle Arabic causative use, distinct from the Classical intransitive khalā bi-, 'to be alone with'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَيْقَظَتْ زَوْجَتِي وَقَدِ انْتَفَضَتْ فَصَارَتْ عِفْرِيتَةً وَحَمَلَتْنِي وَطَلَّعَتْنِي عَلَى جَزِيرَةٍ وَغَابَتْ عَنِّي قَلِيلًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istayqaẓat zawjatī wa-qad intafaḍat fa-ṣārat ʿifrītatan wa-ḥamalatnī wa-ṭallaʿatnī ʿalā jazīratin wa-ghābat ʿannī qalīlan
sentences.l: Then when my wife awoke — she had shuddered and become an ifritah — she carried me and brought me up onto an island, and vanished from me a little while.
sentences.i: When my wife awoke, she gave a sudden shudder and turned into an ifritah; she caught me up, set me down upon an island, and vanished for a little while.
sentences.n: ʿifrītah is simply the feminine of ʿifrīt — the tale's reveal is that his wife is herself a jinniyya of that same formidable class.

sentences.t: وَعَادَتْ عِنْدَ الصَّبَاحِ وَقَالَتْ هَا أَنَا جَارِيَتُكَ أَنَا الَّتِي حَمَلْتُكَ وَنَجَّيْتُكَ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: wa-ʿādat ʿinda al-ṣabāḥi wa-qālat hā anā jāriyatuka anā allatī ḥamaltuka wa-najjaytuka mina al-qatli bi-idhni Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And she returned at daybreak and said: 'Here I am, your slave-girl; I am the one — I carried you and I saved you from death, by the leave of God, Most High.'
sentences.i: She came back at dawn and said, 'Here I am — I am your handmaid, the one who carried you off and saved your life, by the leave of God the Most High.'
sentences.n: anā allatī ḥamaltuka, 'I am the one who [I] carried you', keeps the verb in the first person to agree with anā rather than shifting to 'she' — normal for a relative clause describing a pronoun. jāriyatuka, 'your slave-girl', recalls the guise — a purchased slave-girl — in which he first knew her, before this reveal that she is a jinniyya.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَنِّي جِنِّيَّةٌ فَحَبَّكَ قَلْبِي لِلَّهِ وَأَنَا مُؤْمِنَةٌ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam annī jinniyyatun fa-ḥabbaka qalbī li-llāhi wa-anā muʾminatun bi-Allāhi wa-rasūlihi ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama
sentences.l: And know that I am a jinniyya; so my heart loved you for God's sake, and I am a believer in God and His Messenger — God bless him and grant him peace.
sentences.i: Know that I am a jinniyya; my heart loved you for God's sake alone, for I am a believer in God and His Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace.

sentences.t: فَجِئْتُكَ بِالَّذِي رَأَيْتَنِي فِيهِ فَتَزَوَّجْتَ بِي
sentences.tr: fa-jiʾtuka bi-alladhī raʾaytanī fīhi fa-tazawwajta bī
sentences.l: So I came to you in that which you saw me in, and you married me.
sentences.i: So I came to you in the very form in which you first saw me, and you took me as your wife.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا قَدْ نَجَّيْتُكَ مِنَ الْغَرَقِ وَقَدْ غَضِبْتُ عَلَى إِخْوَتِكَ وَلَابُدَّ أَنْ أَقْتُلَهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā qad najjaytuka mina al-gharaqi wa-qad ghaḍibtu ʿalā ikhwatika wa-lā budda an aqtulahum
sentences.l: And here I am, having already saved you from drowning; and I have grown angry at your brothers, and there is no escape but that I kill them.
sentences.i: And now I have saved you from drowning; but I have grown furious with your brothers, and I mean to kill them, without fail.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ حِكَايَتَهَا تَعَجَّبْتُ وَشَكَرْتُهَا عَلَى فِعْلِهَا وَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَمَّا هَلَاكُ إِخْوَتِي فَلَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu ḥikāyatahā taʿajjabtu wa-shakartuhā ʿalā fiʿlihā wa-qultu lahā ammā halāku ikhwatī fa-lā
sentences.l: So when I heard her story I marveled, and I thanked her for what she had done, and I said to her: 'As for the destruction of my brothers — no.'
sentences.i: When I heard her story I was amazed, and thanked her for what she had done, but I told her, 'As for destroying my brothers — no, that I will not have.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَكَيْتُ لَهَا عَلَى مَا جَرَى لِي مَعَهُمْ مِنْ أَوَّلِ الزَّمَانِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥakaytu lahā ʿalā mā jarā lī maʿahum min awwali al-zamāni ilā ākhirihi
sentences.l: Then I recounted to her all that had happened to me with them, from the first of the time to its end.
sentences.i: Then I told her everything that had passed between me and them, from beginning to end.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَرَفَتْ قَالَتْ أَنَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ أَطِيرُ إِلَيْهِمْ وَأُغْرِقُ مَرْكَبَهُمْ وَأُهْلِكُهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿarafat qālat anā fī hādhihi al-laylati aṭīru ilayhim wa-ughriqu markabahum wa-uhlikuhum
sentences.l: So when she knew, she said: 'I, this very night, will fly to them, and sink their ship, and destroy them.'
sentences.i: When she had learned it all, she said, 'This very night I will fly to them, sink their ship, and destroy them.'

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكِ لَا تَفْعَلِي فَإِنَّ الْمَثَلَ يُقَالُ يَا مُحْسِنُ لِمَنْ أَسَاءَ كَفَى الْمُسِيءَ فِعْلُهُ وَهُمَا إِخْوَتِي عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā bi-Allāhi ʿalayki lā tafʿalī fa-inna al-mathala yuqālu yā muḥsinu li-man asāʾa kafā al-musīʾa fiʿluhu wa-humā ikhwatī ʿalā kulli ḥālin
sentences.l: So I said to her: 'By God, upon you — do not do it! For the proverb is said: O one who does good to him who has done evil, the evildoer's own deed is enough for him. And they are my brothers, in any case.'
sentences.i: I said to her, 'By God, I beg you, do not do it — for as the proverb says: O you who repay evil with good, the wrongdoer's own deed is punishment enough for him. Besides, they are my brothers, whatever has passed.'
sentences.n: The proverb counsels leaving vengeance to the wrongdoer's own deed rather than repaying evil with evil — his crime is felt to carry its own sufficient punishment.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ لَابُدَّ لِي مِنْ قَتْلِهِمْ
sentences.tr: qālat wa-Allāhi lā budda lī min qatlihim
sentences.l: She said: 'By God, there is no escape for me from killing them.'
sentences.i: She said, 'By God, I must kill them.'

sentences.t: فَتَدَخَّلْتُ عَلَيْهَا ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا حَمَلَتْنِي وَطَارَتْ فَوَضَعَتْنِي عَلَى سَطْحِ دَارِي
sentences.tr: fa-tadakhkhaltu ʿalayhā thumma innahā ḥamalatnī wa-ṭārat fa-waḍaʿatnī ʿalā saṭḥi dārī
sentences.l: So I interceded with her; then indeed she carried me and flew off, and set me down upon the roof of my house.
sentences.i: So I pleaded with her; then she took me up and flew off, setting me down on the roof of my own house.

sentences.t: فَتَحْتُ الْأَبْوَابَ وَأَخْرَجْتُ الَّذِي خَبَّيْتُهُ تَحْتَ الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: fataḥtu al-abwāba wa-akhrajtu alladhī khabbaytuhu taḥta al-arḍi
sentences.l: I opened the doors, and I brought out that which I had hidden beneath the ground.
sentences.i: I opened the doors and dug up what I had hidden underground.
sentences.n: khabbaytuhu uses the colloquial verb khabbā, 'to hide', in place of Classical khabaʾa — a Middle Arabic/colloquial form to watch for again.

sentences.t: وَفَتَحْتُ دُكَّانِي بَعْدَ مَا سَلَّمْتُ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَاشْتَرَيْتُ بَضَائِعَ
sentences.tr: wa-fataḥtu dukkānī baʿda mā sallamtu ʿalā al-nāsi wa-ishtaraytu baḍāʾiʿa
sentences.l: And I opened my shop, after I had greeted the people, and I bought goods.
sentences.i: I opened my shop, once I had greeted people, and brought in fresh merchandise.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْعِشَاءُ رَجَعْتُ إِلَى بَيْتِي فَوَجَدْتُ هَذَيْنِ الْكَلْبَيْنِ مَرْبُوطَيْنِ فِي دَارِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-ʿishāʾu rajaʿtu ilā baytī fa-wajadtu hādhayni al-kalbayni marbūṭayni fī dārī
sentences.l: So when it was evening, I returned to my house, and I found these two dogs tied up in my house.
sentences.i: When evening came I went back home, and found these two dogs tied up in my house.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْنِي قَامُوا إِلَيَّ وَبَكَوْا وَتَعَلَّقُوا بِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾawnī qāmū ilayya wa-bakaw wa-taʿallaqū bī
sentences.l: So when they saw me, they rose up to me, and wept, and clung to me.
sentences.i: When they saw me, they sprang up, wept, and clung to me.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَزَوْجَتِي قَالَتْ هَؤُلَاءِ إِخْوَتُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lam ashʿur illā wa-zawjatī qālat hāʾulāʾi ikhwatuka
sentences.l: And I did not perceive except that my wife was saying: 'These are your brothers.'
sentences.i: Before I knew it, my wife was telling me, 'These are your brothers.'
sentences.n: fa-lam ashʿur illā wa-, 'I perceived nothing except that...', is a fixed idiom for a sudden realization — 'before I knew it...'.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ وَمَنْ فَعَلَ بِهِمْ هَذَا الْفِعْلَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu wa-man faʿala bihim hādhā al-fiʿla
sentences.l: So I said: 'And who did this deed to them?'
sentences.i: I said, 'And who did this to them?'

sentences.t: قَالَتْ أَنَا أَرْسَلْتُ إِلَى أُخْتِي فَتَعَلَّتْ بِهِمْ فَذَلِكَ وَمَا يَتَخَلَّصُوا إِلَّا بَعْدَ عَشْرِ سَنَوَاتٍ
sentences.tr: qālat anā arsaltu ilā ukhtī fa-taʿallat bihim fa-dhālika wa-mā yatakhallaṣū illā baʿda ʿashri sanawātin
sentences.l: She said: 'I sent to my sister, and she prevailed upon them; and that is why they will not be freed except after ten years.'
sentences.i: She said, 'I sent word to my sister, and it is she who did this to them; for that, they cannot be freed for ten years.'
sentences.n: fa-taʿallat bihim is an obscure or possibly corrupt form; read here as taʿallat, 'she worked her will/prevailed over them' (root ʿ-l-w), though a slip for fa-faʿalat, 'she did [it] to them', cannot be ruled out. yatakhallaṣū also drops the imperfect plural's final nūn, a recurring Middle Arabic feature in this text.

sentences.t: فَجِيتُ وَأَنَا سَايِرٌ إِلَيْهَا تَخَالُصَهُمْ بَعْدَ إِقَامَتِهِمْ عَشْرِ سَنَوَاتٍ فِي هَذِهِ الْحَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-jītu wa-anā sāyirun ilayhā takhāluṣahum baʿda iqāmatihim ʿashri sanawātin fī hādhihi al-ḥāli
sentences.l: So I came, while I am going to her, [for] their release, after their remaining ten years in this state.
sentences.i: So now I have come, on my way to her, to see to their release, once they have spent these ten years in this condition.
sentences.n: jītu and sāyirun are colloquial forms (for jiʾtu, sāʾirun) that smooth the Classical hamza into a glide — the same feature seen a few lines back in khabbaytuhu. takhāluṣahum, 'their release', is grammatically loose here; the exact construction is uncertain.

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْتُ هَذَا الْفَتَى فَأَخْبَرَنِي بِمَا جَرَى لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾaytu hādhā al-fatā fa-akhbaranī bimā jarā lahu
sentences.l: And I saw this young man, and he told me of what had happened to him.
sentences.i: Along the way I saw this young man, and he told me what had happened to him.

sentences.t: فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ لَا أَبْرَحَ حَتَّى أَنْظُرَ مَا يَجْرِي بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ وَهَذِهِ قِصَّتِي
sentences.tr: fa-aradtu an lā abraḥa ḥattā anẓura mā yajrī baynaka wa-baynahu wa-hādhihi qiṣṣatī
sentences.l: So I resolved not to depart until I should see what would pass between you and him; and this is my story.
sentences.i: So I resolved not to leave until I had seen what would pass between you and him. And that is my story.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْجِنِّيُّ إِنَّهَا حِكَايَةٌ عَجِيبَةٌ وَقَدْ وَهَبْتُ لَكَ ثُلْثَ دَمِهِ وَجِنَايَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-jinniyyu innahā ḥikāyatun ʿajībatun wa-qad wahabtu laka thultha damihi wa-jināyatihi
sentences.l: So the jinni said: 'It is indeed an amazing story; and I have granted you a third of his blood and his crime.'
sentences.i: The jinni said, 'That is indeed an astonishing tale — I grant you a third of his blood and his guilt.'

sentences.t: قَٰلَ الشَّيْخُ الثَّالِثُ صَاحِبُ الْبَغْلَةِ أَنَا أَحْكِي لَكَ حِكَايَةً أَعْجَبَ مِنَ الِاثْنَيْنِ وَ تَهَبُ لِي بَاقِيَ دَمِهِ وَجِنَايَتَهُ أَيُّهَا الْجِنِّيُّ
sentences.tr: qāla al-shaykhu al-thālithu ṣāḥibu al-baghlati anā aḥkī laka ḥikāyatan aʿjaba mina al-ithnayni wa-tahabu lī bāqiya damihi wa-jināyatahu ayyuhā al-jinniyyu
sentences.l: The third sheikh, the master of the mule, said: 'I will tell you a story more amazing than the two, and you will grant me the rest of his blood and his offense, O jinni.'
sentences.i: The third sheikh, the owner of the mule, said, 'I will tell you a tale stranger than these two -- and you will grant me the rest of his blood and his offense, O jinni.'
sentences.n: This mirrors the identical bargain formula used by the first two sheikhs (tahabu li thuluth dami hadha al-tajir), now asking for what remains of the merchant's blood-debt after two-thirds have already been pardoned.

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam
sentences.l: He said: 'Yes.'
sentences.i: He said: 'Yes.'
sentences.n: This third bargain is struck in half a line, without the jinni restating its terms as he did with the first sheikh — the tale trusts the reader to already know the pattern by now.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ أَيُّهَا السُّلْطَانُ وَرَئِيسُ الْجَانِّ إِنَّ هَذِهِ الْبَغْلَةَ كَانَتْ زَوْجَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu ayyuhā al-sulṭānu wa-raʾīsu al-jānni inna hādhihi al-baghlata kānat zawjatī
sentences.l: Then the sheikh said: 'O Sultan, and chief of the jinn, verily this mule was my wife.'
sentences.i: Then the sheikh said: 'O Sultan, chief of the jinn, this mule here was once my wife.'
sentences.n: 'Sultan' addresses the jinni himself, an honorific echoing 'crown of the kings of the jinn' used for the same figure elsewhere in this tale.

sentences.t: فَسَافَرْتُ وَغِبْتُ عَنْهَا سَنَةً كَامِلَةً
sentences.tr: fa-sāfartu wa-ghibtu ʿanhā sanatan kāmilatan
sentences.l: So I traveled, and was absent from her a whole year.
sentences.i: So I set out on a journey and was away from her a whole year.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَضَيْتُ سَفَرِي وَجِيتُ إِلَيْهَا فِي اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: thumma qaḍaytu safarī wa-jītu ilayhā fī al-layli
sentences.l: Then I finished my journey, and came to her at night.
sentences.i: Then, having finished my journey, I came home to her by night.
sentences.n: وَجِيتُ prints the colloquial jītu for Classical jiʾtu, 'I came' — the root's own hamza smoothed away to a bare glide, the same kind of Middle Arabic informality already met in this text's اِيتِنِي for اِئْتِنِي.

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْتُ عَبْدًا أَسْوَدَ رَاقِدًا مَعَهَا فِي الْفِرَاشِ وَهُمْ فِي كَلَامٍ وَغُنْجٍ وَضَحِكٍ وَبَوْسٍ وَهِرَاشٍ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾaytu ʿabdan aswada rāqidan maʿahā fī al-firāshi wa-hum fī kalāmin wa-ghunjin wa-ḍaḥikin wa-bawsin wa-hirāshin
sentences.l: And I saw a black slave, lying with her in the bed, and they were in talk, and coquetry, and laughter, and kissing, and playful scuffling.
sentences.i: And I found a black slave lying with her in the bed, the two of them murmuring, flirting, laughing, kissing, and tussling together.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي عَجِلَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾatnī ʿajilat
sentences.l: And when she saw me, she hastened,
sentences.i: When she caught sight of me, she moved quickly,

sentences.t: وَقَامَتْ إِلَيَّ بِكُوزٍ فِيهِ مَاءٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qāmat ilayya bi-kūzin fīhi māʾun
sentences.l: and rose toward me with a jug, in it water.
sentences.i: and came to me with a jug of water.

sentences.t: فَتَكَلَّمَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَشَّتْنِي وَقَالَتِ اخْرُجْ مِنْ هَذِهِ الصُّورَةِ إِلَى صُورَةِ كَلْبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-takallamat ʿalayhi wa-rashshatnī wa-qālati ukhruj min hādhihi al-ṣūrati ilā ṣūrati kalbin
sentences.l: Then she spoke over it, and sprinkled me, and said: 'Get out of this form, into the form of a dog.'
sentences.i: Then she recited words over it, sprinkled me, and said: 'Out of this shape, into the shape of a dog!'
sentences.n: The imperative اخرج needs no hamza mark at all — it opens with a helping vowel, not a true glottal stop; this is the same transformation-curse formula (get out of this form, into that one) used throughout the tale.

sentences.t: فَصِرْتُ فِي الْحَالِ كَلْبًا فَطَرَدَتْنِي مِنَ الْبَيْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣirtu fī al-ḥāli kalban fa-ṭaradatnī mina al-bayti
sentences.l: So I became, at once, a dog; and she drove me out of the house.
sentences.i: In an instant I became a dog, and she drove me out of the house.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجْتُ مِنَ الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajtu mina al-bābi
sentences.l: So I went out from the door.
sentences.i: And I went out through the door.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ أَزَلْ أَسِيرُ حَتَّى وَصَلْتُ إِلَى دُكَّانِ جَزَّارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lam azal asīru ḥattā waṣaltu ilā dukkāni jazzārin
sentences.l: And I did not cease to journey, until I arrived at a butcher's shop.
sentences.i: I kept moving until I came to a butcher's shop.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمْتُ وَصِرْتُ أكُلُ مِنَ الْعِظَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddamtu wa-ṣirtu ākulu mina al-ʿiẓāmi
sentences.l: So I came forward, and took to eating from the bones.
sentences.i: I went up and began eating from the bones scattered there.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأنِي صَاحِبُ الدُّكَّانِ أَخَذَنِي وَدَخَلَ بِي بَيْتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī ṣāḥibu al-dukkāni akhadhanī wa-dakhala bī baytahu
sentences.l: And when the owner of the shop saw me, he took me, and brought me, with him, into his house.
sentences.i: When the shop's owner saw me, he took me in and brought me home with him.
sentences.n: رَآنِي prints without any hamza indication at all for raʾānī, 'he saw me' — not even the alif-madda that would normally mark the fused hamza-and-long-vowel — as with آكُلُ ('I eat') and أَخِر ('end') later in this same slice.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي بِنْتُ الْجَزَّارِ غَطَّتْ وَجْهَهَا مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾatnī bintu al-jazzāri ghaṭṭat wajhahā minnī
sentences.l: And when the butcher's daughter saw me, she covered her face from me,
sentences.i: But when the butcher's daughter saw me, she covered her face,
sentences.n: Her covering her face from a dog is the tale's own hint that she has already recognized the animal for what it is — an enchanted man, in whose presence an unveiled woman would be improper.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ تَجِيءُ لَنَا بِرَجُلٍ وَتُدْخِلُ بِهِ عَلَيْنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat tajīʾu lanā bi-rajulin wa-tudkhilu bihi ʿalaynā
sentences.l: and said: 'You bring us a man, and bring him in upon us!'
sentences.i: and said, 'You would bring a man to us, and bring him in among us!'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَبُوهَا أَيْنَ الرَّجُلُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla abūhā ayna al-rajulu
sentences.l: So her father said: 'Where is the man?'
sentences.i: So her father said, 'Where is the man?'
