sentences.t: قَالَتْ هَذَا الْكَلْبُ رَجُلٌ سَحَرَتْهُ امْرَأَتُهُ وَأَنَا أَقْدِرُ أُخَلِّصُهُ
sentences.tr: qālat hādhā al-kalbu rajulun saḥarathu imraʾatuhu wa-anā aqdiru ukhalliṣuhu
sentences.l: She said: 'This dog is a man; his wife enchanted him, and I am able to release him.'
sentences.i: She said: 'This dog is really a man — his own wife bewitched him, and I am able to set him free.'

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ أَبُوهَا كَلَامَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa abūhā kalāmahā
sentences.l: And when her father heard her words,
sentences.i: And when her father heard her words,

sentences.t: قَالَ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ يَا بِنْتِي خَلِّصِيهِ
sentences.tr: qāla bi-Allāhi ʿalayka yā bintī khalliṣīhi
sentences.l: he said: 'By God, upon you, my daughter — release him!'
sentences.i: he said: 'By God, I adjure you, my daughter — set him free!'

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْ كُوزًا فِيهِ مَاءٌ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhat kūzan fīhi māʾun
sentences.l: So she took a jug, in it water,
sentences.i: So she took a jug of water,
sentences.n: فاخذت is spelled identically whether it means '(s)he took' or 'I took'; here, continuing straight on from her father's command, it is the daughter who acts, while the very same spelling recurs below (unit 30) as the sheikh's own 'I took' once the narration returns to his voice — the same kind of unpointed ambiguity already met in this corpus for qataltu/qatalta.

sentences.t: وَتَكَلَّمَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَشَّتْ عَلَيَّ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا
sentences.tr: wa-takallamat ʿalayhi wa-rashshat ʿalayya minhu qalīlan
sentences.l: and spoke over it, and sprinkled upon me some of it, a little,
sentences.i: spoke words over it, and sprinkled a little of it upon me,

sentences.t: وَقَالَتِ اخْرُجْ مِنْ هَذِهِ الصُّورَةِ إِلَى صُورَتِكَ الْأُولَى
sentences.tr: wa-qālati ukhruj min hādhihi al-ṣūrati ilā ṣūratika al-ūlā
sentences.l: and said: 'Get out of this form, into your first form.'
sentences.i: and said: 'Out of this shape, back into your own true form!'

sentences.t: فَعُدْتُ إِلَى صُورَتِي الْأُولَى
sentences.tr: fa-ʿudtu ilā ṣūratī al-ūlā
sentences.l: So I returned to my first form,
sentences.i: And I returned to my true form,

sentences.t: فَقَبَّلْتُ يَدَهَا وَقُلْتُ لَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qabbaltu yadahā wa-qultu lahā
sentences.l: and I kissed her hand, and said to her:
sentences.i: and I kissed her hand and said to her:

sentences.t: أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَسْحَرِي زَوْجَتِي كَمَا سَحَرْتِنِي فَأَعْطَتْنِي قَلِيلًا مِنَ الْمَاءِ
sentences.tr: urīdu an tasḥarī zawjatī kamā saḥartinī fa-aʿṭatnī qalīlan mina al-māʾi
sentences.l: 'I want that you enchant my wife, as you enchanted me.' So she gave me a little of the water, and said: 'When
sentences.i: 'I want you to enchant my wife, just as you enchanted me.' So she gave me a little of the water and said: 'When

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ إِذَا رَأَيْتَهَا نَائِمَةً
sentences.tr: wa-qālat idhā raʾaytahā nāʾimatan
sentences.l: you see her asleep,
sentences.i: you see her asleep,

sentences.t: رُشَّ هَذَا الْمَاءَ عَلَيْهَا وَتَكَلَّمْ مَعَهَا بِكَلَامٍ أَرَدْتَهُ
sentences.tr: rushsha hādhā al-māʾa ʿalayhā wa-takallam maʿahā bi-kalāmin aradtahu
sentences.l: sprinkle this water upon her, and speak to her with whatever words you intend,
sentences.i: sprinkle this water on her, and say to her whatever words you wish,

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا تَصِيرُ بِهَا أَنْتَ طَالِبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-innahā taṣīru bihā anta ṭālibun
sentences.l: for she will become, through it, [that] which you are wanting.'
sentences.i: and by it she will turn into whatever you desire.'
sentences.n: The construction anta ṭālib ('you are one wanting') is left loosely attached rather than given a proper predicate for taṣīru; the sense — she will turn into whatever you wish — is clear even where the grammar is not fully worked out.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُ الْمَاءَ وَدَخَلْتُ إِلَى زَوْجَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtu al-māʾa wa-dakhaltu ilā zawjatī
sentences.l: So I took the water, and went in to my wife,
sentences.i: So I took the water and went in to my own wife,

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُهَا نَائِمَةً
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtuhā nāʾimatan
sentences.l: and found her asleep.
sentences.i: and found her asleep.

sentences.t: فَرَشَشْتُ عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءَ وَقُلْتُ اخْرُجِي مِنْ هَذِهِ الصُّورَةِ إِلَى صُورَةِ بَغْلَةٍ فَصَارَتْ فِي الْحَالِ بَغْلَةً
sentences.tr: fa-rashashtu ʿalayhā al-māʾa wa-qultu ukhrujī min hādhihi al-ṣūrati ilā ṣūrati baghlatin fa-ṣārat fī al-ḥāli baghlatan
sentences.l: So I sprinkled the water upon her, and said: 'Get out of this form, into the form of a mule' — and she became, at once, a mule,
sentences.i: I sprinkled the water on her and said: 'Out of this shape, into the shape of a mule!' — and in an instant she became a mule,

sentences.t: وَهِيَ هَذِهِ الَّتِي تَنْظُرُهَا بِعَيْنِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-hiya hādhihi allatī tanẓuruhā bi-ʿaynika
sentences.l: and she is this one whom you see with your own eye,
sentences.i: and this is she, whom you see before you with your own eyes,

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا السُّلْطَانُ وَرَئِيسُ مُلُوكِ الْجَانِّ
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-sulṭānu wa-raʾīsu mulūki al-jānni
sentences.l: O Sultan, and chief of the kings of the jinn.'
sentences.i: O Sultan, chief of the kings of the jinn.'
sentences.n: Here the sheikh's closing address enlarges the jinni's title to 'chief of the kings of the jinn,' echoing the very words the first sheikh used for him at the start of the night ('crown of the kings of the jinn'), though at the opening of his own tale this sheikh had simply said 'chief of the jinn.'

sentences.t: وَقٰلَ لَهَا هَذَا عَجِيبٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā hādhā ʿajībun
sentences.l: And he said to her: 'This is strange.'
sentences.i: And the jinni said to her: 'This is a wonder.'
sentences.n: قل is again the edition's defective spelling of qāla, missing its medial alif, pointed here with the dagger alif; the subject is the jinni, marveling at the mule and addressing her directly, since she cannot answer him in speech.

sentences.t: فَهَزَّتْ رَأْسَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-hazzat raʾsahā
sentences.l: So she shook her head,
sentences.i: So she — the mule — shook her head,

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ بِالْإِشَارَةِ يَعْنِي أَيْ وَاللَّهِ هَذَا حَدِيثِي
sentences.tr: wa-qultu bi-al-ishārati yaʿnī ay wa-Allāhi hādhā ḥadīthī
sentences.l: and I said, by the gesture — meaning: 'Yes, by God!' — this is my story,
sentences.i: and I read her gesture to mean: 'Yes, by God — this is my story,
sentences.n: أَيْ وَاللَّهِ, 'yes, by God,' is a fixed pair of exclamations; the sheikh explains the mule's headshake as though it had voiced this very phrase.

sentences.t: وَمَا جَرَى لِي
sentences.tr: wa-mā jarā lī
sentences.l: and what happened to me.
sentences.i: and what befell me.'

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ حَدِيثِهِ اهْتَزَّ الْجِنِّيُّ مِنَ الطَّرَبِ وَوَهَبَ لَهُ ثُلُثَ دَمِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min ḥadīthihi ihtazza al-jinniyyu mina al-ṭarabi wa-wahaba lahu thulutha damihi
sentences.l: And when he finished his story, the jinni trembled with delight, and granted him a third of his blood.
sentences.i: When he had finished his tale, the jinni shivered with delight and granted him a third of the merchant's blood.
sentences.n: This closes the third and final bargain: with this last third pardoned, the merchant's whole blood-debt is now forgiven, and the frame returns to Shahrazad.

sentences.t: فَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And dawn overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: But dawn overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent, leaving unsaid what she still had leave to tell.
sentences.n: The same night-closing formula as at the end of Night One, rhyming al-ṣabāḥ/al-mubāḥ, recurs essentially unchanged at the end of every night.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا أُخْتُهَا يَا أُخْتِي مَا أَحْلَى حَدِيثَكِ وَأَطْيَبَهُ وَاللَّهِ وَأَعْذَبَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā ukhtuhā yā ukhtī mā aḥlā ḥadīthaki wa-aṭyabahu wa-Allāhi wa-aʿdhabahu
sentences.l: Then her sister said to her: 'O my sister, how sweet is your story, and how pleasant, by God, and how delightful!'
sentences.i: Then her sister said to her: 'O my sister, how sweet your tale is — how pleasant, by God, and how delightful!'

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَأَيْنَ هَذَا مِمَّا أُحَدِّثُكُمْ بِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ الْقَابِلَةَ إِنْ عِشْتُ وَأَبْقَانِي الْمَلِكُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat wa-ayna hādhā mimmā uḥaddithukum bihi al-laylata al-qābilata in ʿishtu wa-abqānī al-maliku
sentences.l: Then she said: 'And where is this, compared with what I shall relate to you on the coming night, if I live and the king lets me remain!'
sentences.i: Then Shahrazad said: 'And this is nothing beside what I shall tell you tomorrow night — if I live, and the king spares me!'
sentences.n: Matches Night One's identical formula for Shahrazad's reply to her sister, closing every night on the same cliffhanging promise.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَقْتُلُهَا حَتَّى أَسْمَعَ بَقِيَّةَ حَدِيثِهَا لِأَنَّهُ عَجِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku wa-Allāhi lā aqtuluhā ḥattā asmaʿa baqiyyata ḥadīthihā li-annahu ʿajībun
sentences.l: Then the king said: 'By God, I will not kill her until I hear the rest of her story, for it is wondrous.'
sentences.i: Then the king said: 'By God, I will not kill her until I have heard the rest of her tale — it is too wondrous to miss.'
sentences.n: Night One's parallel has the king muse this fī nafsihi, 'within himself,' and negates with mā; here the archive omits 'within himself' and negates with lā instead, and adds a new clause, li-annahu ʿajīb ('for it is wondrous'), to justify his mercy this time.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَاتُوا تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ مُتَعَانِقِينَ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: thumma bātū tilka al-laylata mutaʿāniqīna ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: Then they spent that night, embracing one another, until morning.
sentences.i: Then they passed that night together in each other's arms, until morning came.
sentences.n: Compare Night One's identical formula, phrased there as bātū...ilā al-ṣabāḥi mutaʿāniqīna; here the last two elements are reversed, and the narrative connective thumma innahum ('then indeed they') is simplified to a bare thumma.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ الْمَلِكُ مَحَلَّ حُكْمِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja al-maliku maḥalla ḥukmihi
sentences.l: Then the king went out to the place of his judgment,
sentences.i: Then the king went out to his hall of judgment,
sentences.n: Night One's parallel line reads fa-kharaja al-maliku ilā maḥalli ḥukmihi, with the preposition ilā written; here the archive omits it, leaving maḥalla ḥukmihi as a bare accusative of place, vocalized as printed rather than silently restoring the preposition.

sentences.t: وَطَالَعَ الْعَسْكَرَ وَالْوَزِيرَ وَاحْتَبَكَ الدِّيوَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭālaʿa al-ʿaskara wa-al-wazīra wa-iḥtabaka al-dīwānu
sentences.l: and reviewed the army and the vizier, and the council thronged [with people].
sentences.i: and reviewed the troops and received the vizier, while the council chamber filled with people.
sentences.n: ṭālaʿa is the same verb met in the frame story's opening formula (wa-yuṭālaʿa ḥadītha al-umami, 'to peruse the accounts of nations'); here it describes the king reviewing his troops and receiving the vizier — a different morning scene from Night One's account of the vizier's own arrival with the shroud, which this line does not mention.

sentences.t: فَحَكَمَ الْمَلِكُ وَوَلَّى وَعَزَلَ وَنَهَى وَأَمَرَ إِلَى أَخِرِ النَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakama al-maliku wa-wallā wa-ʿazala wa-nahā wa-amara ilā akhiri al-nahāri
sentences.l: Then the king judged, and appointed and dismissed, and forbade and commanded, until the end of the day.
sentences.i: Then the king spent the day dispensing judgment — appointing men to office and removing them, forbidding and commanding — until the day's end.
sentences.n: walla wa-ʿazala is the same idiom for a ruler's routine business of state met in Night One; wa-nahā wa-amara ('forbade and commanded') pairs with it here, the standard formula for wielding authority, elsewhere more often given in the order amara wa-nahā.

sentences.t: فَانْفَضَّ الدِّيوَانُ فَدَخَلَ الْمَلِكُ شَهْرِيَارُ إِلَى قَصْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-infaḍḍa al-dīwānu fa-dakhala al-maliku Shahriyāru ilā qaṣrihi
sentences.l: Then the council dispersed, and King Shahriyar entered his palace.
sentences.i: Then the council broke up, and King Shahriyar went in to his palace.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ قَضَى حَاجَتَهُ مِنْ بِنْتِ الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbala al-laylu qaḍā ḥājatahu min binti al-wazīri
sentences.l: And when night came, he satisfied his need from the vizier's daughter.
sentences.i: And when night fell, he took his fill of the vizier's daughter.
sentences.n: qaḍā ḥājatahu, literally 'he fulfilled his need,' is this text's own euphemism for the king's nightly consummation with his bride before her planned execution — translated here at the same level of directness as the Arabic itself, neither softened nor sharpened.
